approach: Producer writes docs/design/records-history.md (design only), appends D112 (Status Proposed) at the end of docs/decisions.md after D111 in the existing Case/Decision/Alternatives/Tradeoff/Reversal cost/Provenance format, and adds one "Added" bullet under [Unreleased] in CHANGELOG.md. The recommendation is a records branch in this repository (separate root, never merged into main), with a design-level fallback for D72 stealth mode. The document is organised by the request's seven points, plus a measured-vs-estimate list for figures. No code or config changes.

decisions.choice: Recommend a records branch in this repository with a separate root (e.g. refs/athena/records), never merged into main; in D72 stealth mode the same branch lives in a local bare repository in Athena's state directory instead.
decisions.reason: Keeps A5 (records machine-readable, in the repo, full-history secret scan on both histories) and A4 (clone with --mirror/fetch of the ref carries history; lift-out keeps it) with no new service. Git gives fast-forward-only atomic ref updates, so append-only and parallel-writer safety are enforced by the host/push rule rather than invented. Records still verifiably name main commits by hash.

rejected.why: Splits A4 lift-out into two things to move and authenticate, adds a second secret/access surface and a cross-repo atomicity gap; its one gain (hidden from third-party repo, D72) is also met by the stealth-mode local bare repo.

Fails A5 'live in the repo' and 'machine-readable' diffable history unless exported; append-only and secrets scan over history must be rebuilt; lift-out with history needs a dump format; adds a dependency and a new failure class.

rejected.option: Keep records on main and add more exempt entries
rejected.why: This is the status quo that produced six exempt entries and the red check on 02837e0.

decisions.choice: Attribution from records alone: after the host merges, a 'landing' record names the PR head sha, the PR's own commits and the commit the host made on main; main's check walks first-parent main commits and requires each be named by a landing or intervention record. Squash rule at PR level: squash tree equals the PR head tree, and each PR commit is a verified landing or declared intervention from the squash's parent. PR commits are kept reachable by pushing them under refs/athena/pr/<n> (or storing a bundle/tree-and-commit objects in the records branch as a gitlink-free tag/ref) so they survive host deletion.
decisions.reason: Removes the Athena-Verified-Content trailer and fingerprint rules; the record is written after the merge so it can name the host-made commit.

rejected.why: Sri said not to depend on trailers.
Depends on the host, which can garbage-collect or be absent in stealth mode.

decisions.choice: Incremental check: store a checkpoint (last passing main sha, records-branch sha, verifier version) in the records branch; each check judges only commits and records after the checkpoint, plus a scheduled full replay (e.g. nightly/weekly and on verifier-version change) that must reproduce the checkpoint.
decisions.reason: Cost depends on new commits, not ~4,000 records or total commits; replay bounds trust in the checkpoint.

rejected.why: Cache is not shared or auditable and hides drift.

decisions.choice: Migration by copying: one commit on the new root imports every records/ file with a manifest of source paths and content hashes; records/ on main is frozen, then removed only in a late job; commits before the cutover (the six exempt entries, 02837e0) are judged by a frozen 'legacy' rule against a recorded cutover sha, and the exempt list becomes the legacy list in the records history.
decisions.reason: Nothing is moved or rewritten, so reversal is cheap; copy with hash manifest proves completeness.

rejected.why: Violates 'published history on main is never rewritten' (A5).

decisions.choice: Reconciliation: a 'landing intent' record is written before merge (PR number, head); a reconcile step (run at start of any command and by the check) finds main commits with no landing record, looks up the merged PR via the host, and writes the landing record; if the host is unavailable it reports unattributed rather than guessing. Parallel writers: records branch updates are fast-forward-only pushes with compare-and-swap; on rejection fetch, rebase the writer's new files (job-keyed paths, no shared files) and retry; shared append-only files are replaced by per-record files.
decisions.reason: Crash window becomes detectable and repairable from the host's own merge fact.

rejected.option: Write the outcome before merge as today

One Added bullet under [Unreleased] noting the design and the proposed decision.
